name: Kais
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Berry, Keith & Christine Berry. 1987. A survey of the South Bird's Head Stock. Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 4.
earlier_scan.note: SIL survey with phonological data on South Bird's Head languages incl. Kais; plausibly notes stress; no online copy reachable.

sources.citation: Cottet, Fanny. 2015. A phonology of Mbaham: Reduction & contrast. PhD dissertation, Australian National University.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher
sources.note: Contains comparative SBH phonological discussion that names Kais; unlikely but possible remarks on SBH prosody; open but 262 MB scan not fully downloaded here.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31.
sources.note: Entry 53 KAMPONG BARU (Mintamani, Aiso), +-250 speakers, villages, sources Cowan 1953 and Galis 1955; no phonological remarks.

sources.citation: Cowan, H. K. J. 1953. Voorlopige resultaten van een ambtelijk taalonderzoek in Nieuw-Guinea. 's-Gravenhage: Nijhoff (KITLV).
sources.note: Scan pp.28-29, 31, 33 (Delpher scanned): Kampong Baru and Puragi numerals, pronouns, possessive prefixes, imperative particles, basic lexicon and word order from civil-servant manuscript vocabularies; no remark on accent/klemtoon.

sources.citation: de Vries, Lourens. 2024. The linguistic position of the Inanwatan language of West Papua. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia 42: 237-260.
sources.note: p.243: 'Stress is unpredictable in Inanwatan (de Vries 2004: 26) and in Kemberano (Voorhoeve 1985: 7), but we have no information on stress in the other South Bird's Head languages.' Kais is one of those other languages; its Kais data are the Berry & Berry 1987 166-word list. Explicit gap statement, nothing on Kais stress placement.

sources.citation: TransNewGuinea.org, language page 'Kais' (lexical data from de Vries 2024 and Voorhoeve 1975).
sources.note: Lexicon only; led to the de Vries 2024 source. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Holton, Gary & Marian Klamer. 2018. The Papuan languages of East Nusantara and the Bird's Head. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The languages and linguistics of the New Guinea area, 569-640. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Kais appears only in the language table (kzm, SBH, 700, source Smits & Voorhoeve 1998); the stress discussion concerns Timor-Alor-Pantar languages. Nothing on Kais.

sources.citation: de Vries, Lourens. 2004. A short grammar of Inanwatan, an endangered language of the Bird's Head of Papua, Indonesia. Pacific Linguistics 560.
sources.note: Appendix on neighbouring languages lists Kais (600 speakers, Kampong Baru) but states 'Unfortunately, I have no data on Kais.' The stress description (phonemic, unpredictable) is for Inanwatan, a different language.

sources.citation: Berry, Keith & Christine Berry. 1987. A survey of the South Bird's Head Stock. Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 4: 81-117. (SIL/UNCEN)
sources.note: Sec. 3.3 'Phonological features' (p.89) treats only absence of word-final consonants, rare clusters, prenasalised stops, (C)VCV syllable shape; sec. 4.3.1 Kais (p.92) is sociolinguistic (700 speakers, Kais river); Appendix C Kais wordlist carries no stress marks. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Central and Western Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1, 345-460. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Sec. 2.6.2.3.4.1 SBH Family, pp.438-440: locates Kampong Baru on the Kais River, gives pronouns; 'There is almost no grammatical information on all these languages'; the only prosodic remark is for Barau ('the accent is a high-pitch accent'), not Kampong Baru. Nothing on Kais stress.

sources.citation: Cowan, H. K. J. 1960. Nadere gegevens betreffende de verbreiding der West-Papoease taalgroep (Vogelkop, Nieuw-Guinea). Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde 116(3): 350-364.
sources.note: Cites isolated Kpg. Baru lexical forms in cognate comparisons only; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1985. Some notes on the Arandai language. Irian 13: 3-40.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained

sources.note: The only SBH-family stress description besides Inanwatan (Kemberano: unpredictable stress, p.7); not about Kais but the nearest related evidence if a family-level proxy is ever wanted ( is held under aran1237).

sources.citation: Smits, Leo & C. L. Voorhoeve. 1998. The J. C. Anceaux collection of wordlists of Irian Jaya, B: Non-Austronesian (Papuan) languages, Part II. Irian Jaya Source Materials. Leiden/Jakarta: DSALCUL/IRIS.

sources.note: Only unpublished-era primary data on Kampong Baru/Aiso beyond Cowan and Berry; Anceaux's 1950s lists sometimes carry accent diacritics, which would be the sole prosodic evidence for Kais.
